documents.title: Diarrhea
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I've had watery diarrhea for about 3 weeks now. No fever, no blood. It doesn't seem to matter if I eat or not. Feeling crampy and wiped out. Can I get in?

documents.title: RE: Diarrhea

documents.body: Hi Paula, Dr wants to see you. Earliest is Monday 2/12 at 7:40 - booked. Push fluids, an oral rehydration drink is better than plain water. If you feel faint, can't keep fluids down, or see blood, go to urgent care or the ED.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ~4 wks of watery, non-bloody diarrhea, 5-6 times a day, including overnight and on days she barely eats. Mild crampy discomfort, no real pain. No fever, travel, sick contacts, new foods, antibiotics or new meds. No well water - town supply. Lightheaded standing quickly. Weight about the same.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, KCl 40 BID, pantoprazole 40.

O: Temp normal. BP as recorded, HR a bit up. Mucous membranes slightly dry. Abd soft, active bowel sounds, mild diffuse tenderness, no masses. Colonoscopy 6/2023 was normal.

A/P
Chronic watery diarrhea, 1 month. Persists while fasting, which makes a secretory process more likely than osmotic. Long-term PPI noted.
- Stool C. diff, culture, O&P. Celiac serology, TSH, CBC, BMP, Mg.
- Oral rehydration solution, keep potassium as prescribed.
- GI referral now rather than waiting.
Call with worsening, blood, fever, fainting.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - NEW CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 03/19/2024
Reason: chronic watery diarrhea, referred by primary care.

Ms. Nowak, 46, has known primary hyperaldosteronism followed by endocrinology. For several weeks she has had large-volume watery stools that keep coming even on days she fasts. She has cramping in her legs and hands and gets lightheaded. Stool infectious studies, celiac serology and TSH from her PCP were negative. Colonoscopy 06/2023 was normal.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, potassium chloride 40 mEq twice daily, pantoprazole 40 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father hypertension, ruptured cerebral aneurysm at 67; mother type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia; paternal aunt with primary hyperaldosteronism.
Social: never smoker, rare wine, self-employed landscaper.

Exam: dry mucous membranes and decreased skin turgor; she looks volume depleted. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses.

Labs today: potassium 2.0 mEq/L, venous pH 7.30, glucose 150 mg/dL (non-fasting). Stool electrolytes give a low osmotic gap (resulted 03/20).

Addendum 03/19 16:50: potassium of 2.0 called to the patient; she was sent to the hospital infusion unit this evening for intravenous potassium chloride with cardiac monitoring and went home afterward. Her primary care office is asked to repeat a BMP later this week.

Assessment: secretory diarrhea - persists with fasting, low stool osmotic gap - with severe hypokalemia and acidosis from stool losses. Infection, celiac disease and microscopic colitis on a normal colonoscopy are less likely. A hormone-secreting neuroendocrine tumor needs to be excluded.

Plan: CT abdomen with a pancreatic protocol. Continue oral potassium and oral rehydration. Return after imaging.

Outside gastroenterology

documents.title: Repeat potassium

conditions.label: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (VIPoma)
conditions.note: 3.1 cm pancreatic tail mass on CT; hormone confirmed later

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text:
Indication: secretory diarrhea, evaluate for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor.
Technique: multiphase CT of the abdomen with pancreatic protocol (non-contrast, late arterial and portal venous phases) with portal venous imaging of the pelvis. 100 mL IV contrast.
Findings: In the pancreatic tail there is a 3.1 x 2.7 cm well-circumscribed mass that enhances avidly in the late arterial phase and becomes isodense on the portal venous phase. The pancreatic duct is not dilated. The remainder of the pancreas is normal. The splenic vein is patent. The liver is normal in size without focal lesions. Gallbladder, spleen and kidneys are normal. Adrenal glands are unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. Small and large bowel are fluid-filled without wall thickening. No ascites. Pelvic organs are unremarkable.
Bones: no suspicious lesions.
reports.conclusion: 3.1 cm arterially enhancing pancreatic tail mass, most consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. No liver lesions or adenopathy.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Paula with the CT result (copy to us from GI's order). A 3 cm mass in the tail of the pancreas that looks like a neuroendocrine tumor - the kind that can make hormones causing exactly this diarrhea. Nothing in the liver. GI will see her and arrange next tests; most likely surgical removal. She was upset but relieved there's an explanation. Will check in after GI visit. Added to problem list.

medications.sig: 20 mg intramuscular injection every 4 weeks, given in clinic

documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 05/07/2024

Follow-up of secretory diarrhea. CT 04/02 showed a 3.1 cm hypervascular mass in the pancreatic tail without liver lesions. Gallium-68 DOTATATE PET-CT on 05/02 showed intense somatostatin-receptor uptake in the pancreatic tail mass and no other sites of uptake.

She still has 5 to 7 watery stools a day and leg cramps. Potassium improved after IV replacement on her PCP recheck.
Medications: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, potassium chloride 40 mEq BID, pantoprazole 40. NKDA.
Exam: BP 132/84. Not toxic. Abdomen benign.

Assessment: localized, somatostatin-receptor-positive pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor with a secretory diarrhea syndrome.
Plan:
1. Octreotide LAR 20 mg IM every 4 weeks for symptom control, first dose today. Prior authorization obtained by our office.
2. Referral to surgical oncology for resection.
3. Return in a few months; labs then.

documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE SURGICAL ONCOLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 06/11/2024

46-year-old woman with a 3.1 cm pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor on CT and DOTATATE PET-CT, localized, with secretory diarrhea partly controlled on octreotide LAR. Also primary hyperaldosteronism on lisinopril, amlodipine, hydrochlorothiazide and potassium chloride; PUD on pantoprazole. Prior diagnostic laparoscopy at 32. NKDA.

Exam: healthy-appearing. Abdomen soft, small healed laparoscopy scars, no mass.

Assessment and plan: resection is recommended - laparoscopic spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy. Risks discussed, including pancreatic leak and diabetes. Ms. Nowak runs a landscaping business and asked to schedule in November once her season ends; since the tumor is localized and symptoms are controlled on octreotide, this is reasonable. Tentative date 11/19. Continue octreotide through October; electrolytes to be followed by her PCP and GI.

OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 09/30/2024

Ms. Nowak returns for the chronic diarrhea we first evaluated six months ago, in the setting of primary hyperaldosteronism and a pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor awaiting resection on 11/19. On octreotide LAR she still has up to eight bowel movements on bad days; no blood and no abdominal pain. Muscle cramps have come back over the last few weeks. Her weight has held. No travel and no sick contacts.

Medications: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, hydrochlorothiazide 25, potassium chloride 40 mEq BID, pantoprazole 40, octreotide LAR 20 mg every 4 weeks. NKDA.

Exam: BP 110/70, HR 95. Appears dry. Abdomen unremarkable - no masses, no organomegaly.

Labs: sodium 140, potassium 2.9, chloride 95, bicarbonate 32, BUN 18, creatinine 0.9, fasting glucose 90. Stool osmotic gap 50 mOsm/kg. Gastrin normal. Vasoactive intestinal peptide 200 pg/mL (resulted 10/04).

Assessment: functioning pancreatic VIPoma - markedly elevated VIP with secretory diarrhea, gastrin normal - with hypokalemia and volume depletion, compounded by her aldosterone excess and thiazide.
Plan: continue octreotide until surgery; last injection mid-October. Oral rehydration, potassium as prescribed. Surgery 11/19 as planned. We will see her after resection.

events.reason: laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain

reports.text:
Specimen: distal pancreas, laparoscopic spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy.
Gross: segment of distal pancreas 9.0 x 3.5 x 3.0 cm containing a well-circumscribed tan-pink mass, 3.1 cm in greatest dimension.
Microscopic: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor with nested and trabecular growth. Mitoses fewer than 2 per 2 mm2. Ki-67 proliferation index 2%. Immunohistochemistry: synaptophysin and chromogranin positive; vasoactive intestinal peptide positive.
Margins: pancreatic transection and peripancreatic soft tissue margins negative. Lymphovascular invasion not identified.
Lymph nodes: 0 of 8 involved.
reports.conclusion: Well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor, WHO grade 1 (Ki-67 2%), 3.1 cm, VIP immunostain positive, margins negative, 0/8 nodes.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Surgical Oncology
documents.author: surgical oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - SURGICAL ONCOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/19/2024, discharged 11/23/2024.

Diagnosis: pancreatic tail neuroendocrine tumor (VIPoma).
Procedure 11/19: laparoscopic spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy. Estimated blood loss minimal. Drain placed.
Other problems: primary hyperaldosteronism with resistant hypertension, chronic hypokalemia, peptic ulcer disease.
Allergies: NKDA.

Course: uneventful. Diet advanced by day 2. Drain amylase low and drain removed on day 3. Potassium replaced intravenously the first night, then her home oral dose resumed. Blood pressure medicines resumed on day 1. Stools formed by discharge, no watery diarrhea since surgery. Glucose stayed normal.

Pathology: well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor, grade 1, 3.1 cm, Ki-67 2%, VIP positive, margins negative, 0/8 nodes.

Discharge medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, potassium chloride 40 mEq twice daily, pantoprazole 40 mg daily, oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 one tablet every 6 hours as needed (12 tablets). Octreotide discontinued.
Activity: no lifting over 10 lb for 4-6 weeks.
Follow-up: surgical oncology clinic 2 weeks; VIP level at 3 months; surveillance imaging at 1 year; PCP within 2 weeks.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2 wks s/p lap distal pancreatectomy (spleen kept) 11/19. Path: G1 NET, VIP+, clear margins, nodes negative. Saw surgery yesterday - healing well.
The big news: no diarrhea since the operation. 1-2 normal stools a day. Appetite good. Used 3 of the oxycodone pills, now just occasional Tylenol. Doing light greenhouse work only.
Meds: lisinopril 20, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, KCl 40 BID, pantoprazole 40. Octreotide stopped.
Exam: BP as recorded - back up to her pre-tumor baseline now that she's not losing fluid. Afebrile. Port sites clean and dry, no erythema. Abd soft, appropriately tender near the left ports.
A/P
1. VIPoma, resected - surgical onc following; VIP at 3 mo, CT at 1 yr.
2. Primary hyperaldosteronism / resistant HTN / hypokalemia - BP back to 150s; BMP today; continue current regimen.
3. Post-op - lifting limits through early January.
RTC spring physical.
